what_its_for: Adalimumab-adbm is used to treat several conditions where your immune system is overactive and causing inflammation. These conditions include rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis (spine arthritis), Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis in children, and uveitis (eye inflammation). It works by blocking a protein in your body called TNF-alpha that causes inflammation and joint or tissue damage.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a liquid in a pre-filled pen or syringe and is given as a shot (injection) under the skin (subcutaneous). Common injection sites are the front of your thighs or your lower belly, at least 2 inches away from your belly button. Rotate injection sites each time so you do not inject in the same spot twice in a row. Never inject into skin that is bruised, red, tender, hard, or scarred. Let the pen or syringe warm up at room temperature for 15 to 30 minutes before injecting — do not warm it in the microwave or hot water. Clean the injection site with an alcohol wipe and let it dry before injecting. Your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist will teach you how to inject this medicine properly. Do not skip your training before giving yourself the first shot.
dosing: The dose depends on your condition and body weight. Common adult doses are 40 mg every other week for arthritis and skin conditions, or 160 mg on Day 1 followed by 80 mg two weeks later, then 40 mg every other week for Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis. For children, the dose is based on body weight. Always follow the exact dosing schedule your doctor gives you. It may help to mark your injection days on a calendar so you do not forget.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then continue on your regular schedule. If your next scheduled dose is very soon, skip the missed dose and just take the next one as planned. Do not inject two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Keep adalimumab-adbm in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 14 days — keep track of the date you took it out of the refrigerator and throw it away after 14 days if not used. Do not put it back in the refrigerator after it has been stored at room temperature. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens and syringes in an FDA-approved sharps container — never throw them in your regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid close contact with people who are sick, especially those with the flu, chickenpox, or other contagious infections, because this medicine lowers your ability to fight infections. Do not receive live vaccines (such as the nasal flu spray, yellow fever, or shingles vaccine Zostavax) while using this medicine without talking to your doctor first — live vaccines could cause serious infection. Avoid excessive sun exposure and tanning beds, as this medicine may slightly increase your risk of certain skin cancers. Do not start this medicine if you have an active infection of any kind, including tuberculosis (TB). Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially other biologic medicines like etanercept, infliximab, or anakinra, as combining them greatly increases infection risk.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you have: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, sweats, cough, shortness of breath, burning with urination, or a wound that will not heal; signs of TB such as a persistent cough, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss; signs of a nervous system problem such as numbness, tingling, vision changes, weakness, or difficulty walking; signs of heart failure such as sudden weight gain, swelling in your legs or feet, or shortness of breath; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; any new or unusual lumps under your skin; or if you feel much worse or develop new symptoms. Also tell your doctor if you are scheduled for surgery or if you are planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Adalimumab-adbm does not work overnight. Some people start to feel some relief within 2 to 4 weeks, but it may take 3 to 6 months to feel the full benefit of the medicine. It is very important to keep taking it even if you do not notice immediate improvement. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause your condition to flare up.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. If you used this medicine during pregnancy, tell your baby's doctor, because babies exposed to adalimumab-adbm in the womb should not receive live vaccines for up to 5 months after birth. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of this medicine may pass into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine can be used in children as young as 2 years old for certain conditions, with doses based on weight. Older adults: Older adults may have a slightly higher risk of serious infections. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Immunocompromised patients: If your immune system is already weakened for other reasons, you will need especially close monitoring for infections.
